steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...Unauthorized communication. Disclosure of classified information. She is caught in the act.
Hilda hasn't lowered her gun. But in the tense silence, you notice the faint, unmistakable tremor in her hand.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But she's not the mole! Even if she's guilty, she deserves a tribunal, not a summary execution!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't do this, Hilda. Think of Shane. Think of Casey. I know you don't want to live with more regrets.
Her hand moves at last, lifting slightly. The shot rings out, striking the pigeon already in distant flight.
A despairing scream tears from Helene's throat as the blood-soaked pigeon hits the ground, lifeless.
Before the echo fades, Hilda holsters her gun. She strides past the sobbing Helene without a glance and stops squarely in front of you.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Since you are so certain Helene is not the mole... then enlighten me. What is your theory?
You take a deep breath.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: At this point, identifying the real mole has become pretty easy.
First of all...

You're certain of it. Modifying the Monolith prototype into a timed bomb required inside knowledge and access. The saboteur not only survived the guards' attack but is among the small group who worked on restoring and calibrating the prototype.
(−Hilda's Trust)

No... that logic is flawed. Someone had to have modified the Monolith prototype, turning it into a timed bomb. This means the mole not only survived the guards' attack but is also among the small group who worked on restoring and calibrating the prototype.
Second...

options: The mole has a fanatical obsession with the Monolith.
The Monolith isn't actually the mole's true target.

steps.content: This is a core motive. It rules out Nolaine immediately. Her only fixation is Hilda's protection, a goal for which she once considered killing everyone. She has never deviated from this single-minded purpose, making her an impossible candidate.
(−Hilda's Trust)
On second thought, Nolaine once considered killing everyone to protect Hilda. She has never deviated from this single-minded purpose, making her an impossible candidate.
Finally...

options: The mole is intimately familiar with The Wilderness.

steps.content: That's it. The mole used the verses from The Wilderness as a cipher to communicate with Johnson. But Helene, who grew up in DisCity, lacks the literary education that other Outlanders have and wouldn't have read this popular work from over a decade ago. Conversely, Manphist, born in the Outlands and the most experienced and well-read among everyone, would certainly know The Wilderness like the back of his hand.
(−Hilda's Trust)

But that's not quite right. The mole used the verses from The Wilderness as a cipher to communicate with Johnson. But Helene, who grew up in DisCity, lacks the literary education that other Outlanders have and wouldn't have read this popular work from over a decade ago. Conversely, Manphist, born in the Outlands and the most experienced and well-read among everyone, would certainly know The Wilderness like the back of his hand.
The evidence points to one, inescapable conclusion.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...But doesn't that contradict your previous reasoning?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sorry, I misspoke. The real mole is actually...
(Return to previous choice)
Option B: The mole is Helene.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Yingying

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Are you thinking straight?
(Return to previous choice)
Option C: The mole is Manphist.
As one, you and Hilda fix your stares on Manphist. He looks back at you, his face the very picture of innocence.
In response to your silent accusation, he offers nothing but a resigned shrug.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Ah, of course. I suppose it was inevitable. By simple process of elimination, I am the last and most logical suspect.

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: But is it not a rather unscientific method to condemn a man based solely on that, without a single piece of tangible proof?

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: Consider this: if guards we dismissed could orchestrate an assault, is it not equally plausible that an actor, entirely unknown to us, remains hidden within the manor's shadows?

steps.speaker: Manphist
steps.content: And the modifications to the Monolith... Surely, someone could have accessed the room while Hilda was absent to make the alterations?

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: It's alright.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: We'll have our answers soon enough. The interrogation will see to that.
